legalRights.summary: Japan allows police to detain suspects for up to 23 days before formal charges. You have the right to contact your embassy and request a lawyer, but lawyers cannot be present during police interrogation. Japan's conviction rate exceeds 99% — exercise your right to silence.
legalRights.maxDetentionNotes: 48h police custody → 10-day prosecutorial extension → 10-day re-extension → up to 3 additional days. Total: 23 days before charges must be filed or you're released.
legalRights.lawyerDuringInterrogationNotes: Your lawyer can visit you in the detention facility but cannot sit in during questioning. This is unusual by Western standards.
legalRights.embassyContactNotes: Police must notify your embassy upon request (Vienna Convention). Say: 大使館に連絡してください (Taishikan ni renraku shite kudasai)
legalRights.rightToSilenceNotes: Constitutionally guaranteed (Article 38). Exercise it. Police may pressure you to talk — you are not required to answer any questions.
legalRights.interpreterNotes: Free interpreter provided for interrogation. Quality varies — request your embassy's recommended interpreter if possible.

keyDosAndDonts.text: Immediately request to contact your embassy
State clearly: 'I want a lawyer' — 弁護士が必要です (Bengoshi ga hitsuyō desu)
Exercise your right to remain silent until a lawyer is present
Stay calm and respectful — demeanor matters greatly in Japanese legal proceedings
Ask for all documents in your language before signing anything
Do NOT sign any document you cannot fully read and understand in your own language
Do NOT make any admissions, even casually — everything can be used as evidence
Do NOT physically resist — assault on an officer is a separate serious charge
Do NOT agree to 'voluntary' questioning without a lawyer — it's still recorded

legalRights.localLawyerHotline: Japan Legal Support Center (Houterasu): 0570-078377 (multilingual, Mon-Fri 9am-9pm, Sat 9am-5pm)
commonOffensesForTourists: Drug possession (zero tolerance — even trace amounts of marijuana)
Photography in restricted areas (shrines, certain neighborhoods)
legalRights.bailNotes: Bail is rarely granted to foreigners during the initial 23-day detention period. After formal charges, bail becomes possible but is not guaranteed.
legalRights.policeReportProcess: Go to the nearest police box (交番 kōban) or police station (警察署 keisatsusho). Ask for English support — larger stations have multilingual officers. You'll receive a 受理番号 (juri bangō — receipt number) which is required for insurance claims. Process takes 1-3 hours.
sources: US Embassy Tokyo — Arrest of a US Citizen

protocols.alertSystem: J-Alert (nationwide) + Earthquake Early Warning (緊急地震速報) pushed to all smartphones automatically
protocols.alertAppOffline: Safety Tips (NTA) — works offline, push alerts in English
immediateActions: DROP to hands and knees
Take COVER under sturdy furniture or against interior wall
HOLD ON until shaking stops
Stay away from windows, heavy objects, exterior walls
If outdoors: move to open area away from buildings, power lines, trees
If driving: pull over, stay in car, avoid bridges and overpasses
afterActions: Check for injuries — apply first aid
Expect aftershocks — can be nearly as strong as the main quake
If near coast, move to high ground immediately (tsunami risk)
Check gas lines — turn off main valve if you smell gas
Tune to NHK World (English) for official updates
Head to nearest designated evacuation site if building is damaged
protocols.shelterInfo: Designated evacuation sites (避難所 hinanjo) are at schools, parks, and community centers — marked with green signs showing a running figure. Pre-cache your area in Google Maps for offline use.

protocols.alertSystem: J-Alert + tsunami warning sirens along all coastlines
immediateActions: Move INLAND and UPHILL immediately — do NOT wait for an official warning if you feel strong shaking near the coast
Get above 30m / 100ft elevation if possible
If in a concrete building and cannot evacuate: go to 3rd floor or higher
Never go to the beach to watch — waves move faster than you can run
If in a boat at sea: head to deep open water
afterActions: Stay at high ground for hours — multiple waves can arrive, and later waves are often larger
Do NOT return to coast until the official all-clear is issued
Avoid flooded areas — debris, chemical contamination, structural collapse risk
Listen to NHK World for all-clear announcement
protocols.shelterInfo: Tsunami evacuation towers (津波避難タワー) and tsunami evacuation buildings (津波避難ビル) exist in coastal towns. Follow blue directional signs pointing uphill. Most coastal towns have marked evacuation routes.
protocols.localPhrase: 津波！高台へ逃げて！(Tsunami! Takadai e nigete!) — Tsunami! Run to high ground!

protocols.alertSystem: Japan Meteorological Agency (JMA) warnings via TV, radio, and smartphone push notifications
protocols.alertAppOffline: Safety Tips (NTA) + NHK World app (cache forecasts)
immediateActions: Stay indoors, away from windows
Stock water and food for 2-3 days before the typhoon arrives
Charge all devices fully
Move to upper floors if flooding is expected
Secure or bring in any outdoor items that could become projectiles
afterActions: Avoid downed power lines and flooded roads
Watch for landslides if in mountainous or hilly areas
Trains will likely be suspended — check Hyperdia, Jorudan, or railway apps for service status
Flights may be cancelled for 24-48h — contact airline early
protocols.shelterInfo: Same evacuation centers as earthquakes. Hotels shelter guests in place. If your accommodation is in a flood zone, relocate before the typhoon hits.
protocols.localPhrase: 台風が来ます (Taifū ga kimasu) — A typhoon is coming

protocols.alertSystem: JMA Volcanic Alert Levels (1-5) broadcast via J-Alert and local authorities
immediateActions: Move away from the volcano — follow evacuation orders immediately
Cover nose and mouth with cloth to avoid inhaling ash
If caught in ashfall: seek shelter indoors, close all windows and doors
Protect eyes — volcanic ash causes severe irritation
Do NOT drive through heavy ashfall — engines can seize
afterActions: Clear ash from roof if accumulation is heavy (collapse risk)
Avoid river valleys — lahars (volcanic mudflows) can travel far from the crater
Monitor JMA updates for ongoing eruption status
protocols.shelterInfo: Each active volcano has designated evacuation zones and shelter areas. If hiking near active volcanoes (Fuji, Aso, Sakurajima), check the current alert level before departure.
protocols.localPhrase: 噴火！逃げて！(Funka! Nigete!) — Eruption! Run!
